````text
# #4542: Patch: the WebAssembly module's Duos code is compiled, linted and tested in CI, not only by the local dev server
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The browser's copy of the game engine has a section that plays four-player co-op games. Only a developer's local test page uses it, and only the local dev server builds it. No check on a pull request ever compiles that section, lints it or calls it. So a change to the co-op rules that breaks it would pass every check and merge, and the next person to start the dev server would find it broken. Once this is built, every test run compiles that section and a test plays a co-op game through it. It still ships in no module a player loads.

## Why
- The Duos bodies are about 110 lines behind `#[cfg(feature = "duos")] mod duos_bodies` (`crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs:925-1033`): `duos_create`, `duos_begin`, `duos_reduce`, `duos_legal_actions`, `duos_view_for` and their setup check. Without the feature, stubs answer that the module was built without it (`lib.rs:1035`).
- Only the `predev` script at `apps/web/package.json:14` turns the feature on (`JACKIOH_WASM_DUOS=1`, `scripts/build-wasm.sh:172`). Everything else builds without it:
  - the web's `pretest`, `prebuild` and `prebuild:e2e` (`package.json:17-27`);
  - every workflow's run of `build-wasm.sh`;
  - clippy and every `cargo test` group.
  A grep of `.github/`, `scripts/` and every `Cargo.toml` finds no other `duos` feature and no other `JACKIOH_WASM_DUOS=1`.
- The tests that exist never touch the real bodies:
  - The only Rust test of the Duos exports, `duos_exports_answer_what_the_core_bodies_answer` (`crates/wasm/c/src/tests.rs:674`), checks the stub; its comment says 'Built without the duos feature each body answers the reason'.
  - The web's test of the exports (`apps/web/src/wasm/index.test.ts`) uses fake bindings.
  - e2e's Duos specs (41, 55) play through the server.
- `crates/engine/src/duos`, the engine module these bodies call, changed in 10 commits since August, and nothing would say if one of them broke the bodies.
- #4426 closed the same kind of gap for the `ts` features with a dev-dependency (`crates/wasm/core/Cargo.toml:26-32`). `ts_the_generated_types_are_written_by_the_ci_test_build` (`crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs:3437`) keeps that dev-dependency in place.

## Proposal
1. Turn `jackioh-wasm-core`'s `duos` feature on through a `[dev-dependencies]` line, as #4426 did for `ts`. The C module's crate, `crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml`, is the natural home. Dev-dependency features reach every workspace test build and every `--all-targets` clippy build. They never reach the release binaries or the modules `build-wasm.sh` makes, so the shipped modules keep their stubs.
2. Replace the stub test with one that plays a short Duos game through the C exports, comparing each answer with `jackioh_engine::duos` called directly:
   - create from a seeded options literal, and begin;
   - list one seat's actions and reduce one listed action;
   - view each of the four seats.
   Add one bad deck, refused with its seat named.
3. Add a test in `acceptance.rs`, beside the `ts` one, that fails if the dev-dependency line is removed.

## Where it lands
- `crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml` (or `crates/wasm/core/Cargo.toml`): `[dev-dependencies]`
- `crates/wasm/c/src/tests.rs`
- `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`
- `crates/wasm/README.md`'s note on the `duos` feature (its line 78)
- SPEC §13 (Duos) is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` compile `duos_bodies`. A reviewer can confirm it: a type error planted in the module fails both.
- [ ] A test plays create, begin, legal actions, reduce and the four seats' views through the C exports, and each answer equals the engine's own. A bad Duos deck is refused naming its seat.
- [ ] `JACKIOH_WASM_C=1 JACKIOH_WASM_NORMAL=0 sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` and the default `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` still build the stubs: their `duos_create` still answers that the module was built without the feature.
- [ ] Removing the dev-dependency line fails an `acceptance.rs` test, in the pattern #4426 set.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

## Size and risks
Medium but small: three or four files, about 80 to 120 lines. If the bodies no longer compile, or no longer agree with the engine, the first build says so, and the fix stays in `crates/wasm/core`. Afterwards the stubs compile only in the WebAssembly builds of the `web` job, which already builds them on every pull request it runs for.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45093755555)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Every `cargo test` and `--all-targets` clippy build compiles the real Duos bodies in `crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs` (`duos_create`, `duos_begin`, `duos_reduce`, `duos_legal_actions`, `duos_view_for`) by turning `jackioh-wasm-core`'s `duos` feature on through a `[dev-dependencies]` line, as #4426 did for `ts`. A rewritten C-export test plays a short Duos game through the real bodies and compares each answer with the core bodies, plus a bad-deck refusal naming its seat; an `acceptance.rs` test fails if the line is removed. The modules `scripts/build-wasm.sh` makes keep their stubs.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml` | change | `[dev-dependencies]`: one line, `jackioh-wasm-core` with `features = ["duos"]`, plus its `#4542` comment |
| `crates/wasm/c/src/tests.rs` | change | Replace `duos_exports_answer_what_the_core_bodies_answer` (`:674`) with a real-bodies game test |
| `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` | change | New `dev_dependency_missing_duos` scanner plus two tests beside the `ts` ones (`:3437`, `:3449`) |
| `crates/wasm/README.md` | change | One sentence in "Build and the client's seams" (`:78-81`) noting the dev-dependency |

Do not touch: `.github/`, `scripts/build-wasm.sh`, `apps/web/package.json`, `crates/wasm/Cargo.toml`, `crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs` (unless the first build shows the bodies broke against the engine — then the fix stays there and nowhere else), anything under `crates/engine/`, anything under `spec/` (SPEC §13 is unchanged; this makes no rules decision, so no ruling note, no `rN_` test, no `spec/pending` paragraph), `apps/web/src/wasm/index.test.ts`, e2e Duos specs.

## Steps

1. `crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml`: in `[dev-dependencies]`, after the `jackioh-shared` line, add:
   ```toml
   # #4542: turns `jackioh-wasm-core`'s `duos` feature on in every test build, so
   # `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` compile the real
   # Duos bodies. Dev-dependency features never reach the WebAssembly modules
   # `scripts/build-wasm.sh` makes, so the shipped modules keep their stubs.
   # `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` holds this line.
   jackioh-wasm-core = { path = "../core", features = ["duos"] }
   ```
   It must be this file, not `crates/wasm/core/Cargo.toml`: a crate cannot enable its own feature from its own dev-dependencies. Repeating the existing `[dependencies]` path entry under `[dev-dependencies]` with features is allowed; Cargo unifies them in test builds only.
2. `crates/wasm/c/src/tests.rs`: delete `duos_exports_answer_what_the_core_bodies_answer` (`:673-692`) and write `duos_exports_play_a_game_through_the_core_bodies` in its place, reusing the file's `init`, `call!`, `expect`, `ok` helpers and `game()`'s deck-building pattern (`:70-77`). No new imports: `json!`, `Value`, `STATUS_OK`, `STATUS_FAILED` are already in scope:
   - Build four decks: for seeds `"duos-c-a1"`, `"duos-c-a2"`, `"duos-c-b1"`, `"duos-c-b2"`, send `json!({ "rngSeed": seed, "size": jackioh_engine::config::DECK_SIZE }).to_string()` through `call!(build_ai_deck; options;)` and keep each answer's `["deck"]`.
   - `options = json!({ "seed": "duos-c-test", "decks": { "a1": …, "a2": …, "b1": …, "b2": … } }).to_string()` (camelCase keys, no `catalog`: the bodies fall back to the registered catalog). Assert `call!(duos_create; options;)` equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_create(&options))` and unwrap it with `ok` into `created`.
   - `begun = ok(call!(duos_begin; created;))`, assert it equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_begin(&created))`; parse as `Value`, keep `state = begun["state"].to_string()` (same envelope handling as `game()` `:79-80`).
   - For each seat in `["a1", "a2", "b1", "b2"]`, assert `call!(duos_legal_actions; state, seat;)` equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_legal_actions(&state, seat))`; parse each list, take the first seat with a non-empty list, and assert one exists ("a begun duos game offers an action").
   - `action = json!({ "seat": seat, "nonce": "duos-c-1", "body": bodies[0] }).to_string()` (`DuosAction` shape: `wire/duos.rs:313`; seat serializes as `"a1"`). Assert `call!(duos_reduce; state, action;)` equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_reduce(&state, &action))`, has `STATUS_OK`, and its text holds no `"error"`.
   - For each of the four seats, assert `call!(duos_view_for; state, seat;)` equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_view_for(&state, seat))` with `STATUS_OK`.
   - Bad deck: clone the options JSON with `b2` replaced by `[]`; assert the answer equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_create(&bad))`, has `STATUS_FAILED`, and its text contains `"b2"` (the setup check labels each deck by seat: `core/src/lib.rs:966-982`; `validate_deck`'s message starts with the label, e.g. `b2: deck must hold exactly 25 cards`).
3. `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`: copy the `ts` pattern at `:3408-3473`. Add `fn dev_dependency_missing_duos(manifest: &str) -> bool` right after `dev_dependencies_missing_ts`: scan the `[dev-dependencies]` section exactly as that function does (strip `#` comments, track the section header), return false only when a line starts with `jackioh-wasm-core`, has `=`, and contains both `features` and `"duos"`. Add `duos_the_c_test_build_compiles_the_duos_bodies` after `ts_the_generated_types_are_written_by_the_ci_test_build`: read `repo().join("crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml")`, assert `!dev_dependency_missing_duos(&manifest)` with a message naming the file and telling the reader to restore the `features = ["duos"]` line. Add `duos_the_dev_dependency_scan_finds_a_dropped_feature` after `ts_the_dev_dependency_scan_finds_a_dropped_feature` with inline manifests: ok line, line without features, commented-out line, `duos` only under `[dependencies]`, no dev section — mirroring the five `ts` cases.
4. `crates/wasm/README.md`: at the end of the `duos` paragraph (`:78-81`), append one sentence: test and lint builds compile the real bodies through `jackioh-wasm-c`'s dev-dependency on `jackioh-wasm-core`'s `duos` feature (`crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml`, held by `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`); every module `scripts/build-wasm.sh` makes still builds the stubs.
5. If step 2's first build fails inside `duos_bodies` (the issue warns 10 engine commits may have broken them), fix `crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs:925-1033` only, against `jackioh_engine::duos`'s current signatures. Do not change the engine to fit the bodies.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c duos_exports_play_a_game_through_the_core_bodies` — the new game test; fails on stubs (`duos_create` would refuse valid options) and on any body/engine disagreement.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` — whole C crate, guards the other export tests.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance -- duos_the ts_the` — both new scanner tests plus the neighboring `ts` tests.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm --test export_parity` — export lists are feature-independent (it reads sources), confirm it stays green.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-wasm-c --all-targets -- -D warnings` — proves lint covers `duos_bodies` (dev-deps are built for `--all-targets`).
- `cargo build -p jackioh-wasm-c` — fast stub check: `cargo build` ignores dev-dependencies, so this must still compile the stubs.
- `cargo fmt --check`.
- The two full `scripts/build-wasm.sh` invocations (default and `JACKIOH_WASM_C=1 JACKIOH_WASM_NORMAL=0`) and the planted-type-error check are CI's and the reviewer's respectively (the `web (wasm c module)` job; a cold C-module build is ~8 minutes) — do not run them here; the `cargo build` line above plus the fact that the only `features = ["duos"]` line sits under `[dev-dependencies]` is this build's stub evidence.

## Done when

- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-wasm-c --all-targets -- -D warnings` compile the real `duos_bodies` (the new test passing proves it; a planted type error would fail both).
- [ ] The new test plays create, begin, legal actions, reduce, and all four seats' views through the C exports with each answer equal to the core body's, and a bad deck is refused naming its seat.
- [ ] `cargo build -p jackioh-wasm-c` still compiles the stubs; no `build-wasm.sh` output changes.
- [ ] Deleting the dev-dependency line fails `duos_the_c_test_build_compiles_the_duos_bodies`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance -- duos_the ts_the`, `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm --test export_parity`, and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

## Risks

- Feature unification: workspace-wide `--all-targets` builds now compile core with `duos` for other members' test graphs too. Harmless: they are the same bodies the dev server ships, and `export_parity` reads sources, not features.
- `build_ai_deck` decks are seed-deterministic; fixed seeds keep the test stable. If AI-deck generation ever refuses Duos validation, build decks from `DECK_SIZE` copies of a known catalog id instead — but try AI decks first, they are this file's idiom.
- Views leak nothing new: the test only compares C-export bytes against core-body bytes, never against a hand-written expectation.
- No spec or catalog impact: no ruling note, no pending fragment, no wire-type change.

## Open questions

None. Every decision above follows the issue or the #4426 precedent; the only fork (Cargo.toml location) is settled in step 1 with its reason.
````

## Goal

Every `cargo test` and `--all-targets` clippy build compiles the real Duos bodies in `crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs` (`duos_create`, `duos_begin`, `duos_reduce`, `duos_legal_actions`, `duos_view_for`) by turning `jackioh-wasm-core`'s `duos` feature on through a `[dev-dependencies]` line, as #4426 did for `ts`. A rewritten C-export test plays a short Duos game through the real bodies and compares each answer with the core bodies, plus a bad-deck refusal naming its seat; an `acceptance.rs` test fails if the line is removed. The modules `scripts/build-wasm.sh` makes keep their stubs.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml` | change | `[dev-dependencies]`: one line, `jackioh-wasm-core` with `features = ["duos"]`, plus its `#4542` comment |
| `crates/wasm/c/src/tests.rs` | change | Replace `duos_exports_answer_what_the_core_bodies_answer` (`:674`) with a real-bodies game test |
| `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` | change | New `dev_dependency_missing_duos` scanner plus two tests beside the `ts` ones (`:3437`, `:3449`) |
| `crates/wasm/README.md` | change | One sentence in "Build and the client's seams" (`:78-81`) noting the dev-dependency |

Do not touch: `.github/`, `scripts/build-wasm.sh`, `apps/web/package.json`, `crates/wasm/Cargo.toml`, `crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs` (unless the first build shows the bodies broke against the engine — then the fix stays there and nowhere else), anything under `crates/engine/`, anything under `spec/` (SPEC §13 is unchanged; this makes no rules decision, so no ruling note, no `rN_` test, no `spec/pending` paragraph), `apps/web/src/wasm/index.test.ts`, e2e Duos specs.

## Steps

1. `crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml`: in `[dev-dependencies]`, after the `jackioh-shared` line, add:
   ```toml
   # #4542: turns `jackioh-wasm-core`'s `duos` feature on in every test build, so
   # `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` compile the real
   # Duos bodies. Dev-dependency features never reach the WebAssembly modules
   # `scripts/build-wasm.sh` makes, so the shipped modules keep their stubs.
   # `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` holds this line.
   jackioh-wasm-core = { path = "../core", features = ["duos"] }
   ```
   It must be this file, not `crates/wasm/core/Cargo.toml`: a crate cannot enable its own feature from its own dev-dependencies. Repeating the existing `[dependencies]` path entry under `[dev-dependencies]` with features is allowed; Cargo unifies them in test builds only.
2. `crates/wasm/c/src/tests.rs`: delete `duos_exports_answer_what_the_core_bodies_answer` (`:673-692`) and write `duos_exports_play_a_game_through_the_core_bodies` in its place, reusing the file's `init`, `call!`, `expect`, `ok` helpers and `game()`'s deck-building pattern (`:70-77`). No new imports: `json!`, `Value`, `STATUS_OK`, `STATUS_FAILED` are already in scope:
   - Build four decks: for seeds `"duos-c-a1"`, `"duos-c-a2"`, `"duos-c-b1"`, `"duos-c-b2"`, send `json!({ "rngSeed": seed, "size": jackioh_engine::config::DECK_SIZE }).to_string()` through `call!(build_ai_deck; options;)` and keep each answer's `["deck"]`.
   - `options = json!({ "seed": "duos-c-test", "decks": { "a1": …, "a2": …, "b1": …, "b2": … } }).to_string()` (camelCase keys, no `catalog`: the bodies fall back to the registered catalog). Assert `call!(duos_create; options;)` equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_create(&options))` and unwrap it with `ok` into `created`.
   - `begun = ok(call!(duos_begin; created;))`, assert it equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_begin(&created))`; parse as `Value`, keep `state = begun["state"].to_string()` (same envelope handling as `game()` `:79-80`).
   - For each seat in `["a1", "a2", "b1", "b2"]`, assert `call!(duos_legal_actions; state, seat;)` equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_legal_actions(&state, seat))`; parse each list, take the first seat with a non-empty list, and assert one exists ("a begun duos game offers an action").
   - `action = json!({ "seat": seat, "nonce": "duos-c-1", "body": bodies[0] }).to_string()` (`DuosAction` shape: `wire/duos.rs:313`; seat serializes as `"a1"`). Assert `call!(duos_reduce; state, action;)` equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_reduce(&state, &action))`, has `STATUS_OK`, and its text holds no `"error"`.
   - For each of the four seats, assert `call!(duos_view_for; state, seat;)` equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_view_for(&state, seat))` with `STATUS_OK`.
   - Bad deck: clone the options JSON with `b2` replaced by `[]`; assert the answer equals `expect(wasm_core::duos_create(&bad))`, has `STATUS_FAILED`, and its text contains `"b2"` (the setup check labels each deck by seat: `core/src/lib.rs:966-982`; `validate_deck`'s message starts with the label, e.g. `b2: deck must hold exactly 25 cards`).
3. `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`: copy the `ts` pattern at `:3408-3473`. Add `fn dev_dependency_missing_duos(manifest: &str) -> bool` right after `dev_dependencies_missing_ts`: scan the `[dev-dependencies]` section exactly as that function does (strip `#` comments, track the section header), return false only when a line starts with `jackioh-wasm-core`, has `=`, and contains both `features` and `"duos"`. Add `duos_the_c_test_build_compiles_the_duos_bodies` after `ts_the_generated_types_are_written_by_the_ci_test_build`: read `repo().join("crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml")`, assert `!dev_dependency_missing_duos(&manifest)` with a message naming the file and telling the reader to restore the `features = ["duos"]` line. Add `duos_the_dev_dependency_scan_finds_a_dropped_feature` after `ts_the_dev_dependency_scan_finds_a_dropped_feature` with inline manifests: ok line, line without features, commented-out line, `duos` only under `[dependencies]`, no dev section — mirroring the five `ts` cases.
4. `crates/wasm/README.md`: at the end of the `duos` paragraph (`:78-81`), append one sentence: test and lint builds compile the real bodies through `jackioh-wasm-c`'s dev-dependency on `jackioh-wasm-core`'s `duos` feature (`crates/wasm/c/Cargo.toml`, held by `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`); every module `scripts/build-wasm.sh` makes still builds the stubs.
5. If step 2's first build fails inside `duos_bodies` (the issue warns 10 engine commits may have broken them), fix `crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs:925-1033` only, against `jackioh_engine::duos`'s current signatures. Do not change the engine to fit the bodies.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c duos_exports_play_a_game_through_the_core_bodies` — the new game test; fails on stubs (`duos_create` would refuse valid options) and on any body/engine disagreement.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` — whole C crate, guards the other export tests.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance -- duos_the ts_the` — both new scanner tests plus the neighboring `ts` tests.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm --test export_parity` — export lists are feature-independent (it reads sources), confirm it stays green.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-wasm-c --all-targets -- -D warnings` — proves lint covers `duos_bodies` (dev-deps are built for `--all-targets`).
- `cargo build -p jackioh-wasm-c` — fast stub check: `cargo build` ignores dev-dependencies, so this must still compile the stubs.
- `cargo fmt --check`.
- The two full `scripts/build-wasm.sh` invocations (default and `JACKIOH_WASM_C=1 JACKIOH_WASM_NORMAL=0`) and the planted-type-error check are CI's and the reviewer's respectively (the `web (wasm c module)` job; a cold C-module build is ~8 minutes) — do not run them here; the `cargo build` line above plus the fact that the only `features = ["duos"]` line sits under `[dev-dependencies]` is this build's stub evidence.

## Done when

- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-wasm-c --all-targets -- -D warnings` compile the real `duos_bodies` (the new test passing proves it; a planted type error would fail both).
- [ ] The new test plays create, begin, legal actions, reduce, and all four seats' views through the C exports with each answer equal to the core body's, and a bad deck is refused naming its seat.
- [ ] `cargo build -p jackioh-wasm-c` still compiles the stubs; no `build-wasm.sh` output changes.
- [ ] Deleting the dev-dependency line fails `duos_the_c_test_build_compiles_the_duos_bodies`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance -- duos_the ts_the`, `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm --test export_parity`, and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

## Risks

- Feature unification: workspace-wide `--all-targets` builds now compile core with `duos` for other members' test graphs too. Harmless: they are the same bodies the dev server ships, and `export_parity` reads sources, not features.
- `build_ai_deck` decks are seed-deterministic; fixed seeds keep the test stable. If AI-deck generation ever refuses Duos validation, build decks from `DECK_SIZE` copies of a known catalog id instead — but try AI decks first, they are this file's idiom.
- Views leak nothing new: the test only compares C-export bytes against core-body bytes, never against a hand-written expectation.
- No spec or catalog impact: no ruling note, no pending fragment, no wire-type change.

## Open questions

None. Every decision above follows the issue or the #4426 precedent; the only fork (Cargo.toml location) is settled in step 1 with its reason.
